Two-level mediation: a step-by-step workflow

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-twolevel-tutorial.qmd

This guide walks one analysis from a lavaan fit to a reported result, and says what to check at each step. It uses the same simulated data as Two-level mediation, which is the reference page for every option; read that page when a step here needs more detail. The route needs lavaan (Suggests).

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
has_lavaan <- requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)

Step 1: fit the same regressions at both levels

Treatment, mediator and outcome are measured on level-1 units nested in clusters. Write the same three regressions at level: 1 (within) and level: 2 (between) and fit with cluster =.

set.seed(2026)
J <- 100
n <- 5
id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
xb <- rnorm(J)[id]
xw <- rnorm(J * n)
x <- xb + xw
m <- 0.4 * xw + 0.7 * xb + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(m, id)
y <- 0.3 * xw + 0.2 * xb + 0.5 * (m - mbar) + 0.9 * mbar + 0.5 * rnorm(J)[id] + rnorm(J * n)
d <- data.frame(id = id, X = x, M = m, Y = y)

model <- "
  level: 1
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
  level: 2
    M ~ X
    Y ~ M + X
"
fit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = d, cluster = "id")

Step 2: extract, then check the fit before reading any effect

extract_mediation() reads the fit and never refits. Name the three roles; the paths are found by variable name and level, not by label.

td <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y")

Three properties decide whether the between-level numbers can be trusted. Read them first.

td@icc
        X         M         Y
0.5031045 0.3233019 0.4001454 
td@between_identified
[1] TRUE
td@admissible
[1] TRUE
td@n_clusters
[1] 100
td@cross_level_equal
character(0)
Check What it means If it fails
between_identified the treatment and the mediator vary enough between clusters (ICC at least 0.01) only the within effects are returned; between effects and the contrast stop with class medfit_between_unidentified
admissible lavaan’s post-check passed (no negative variance) inspect the fit; standard errors on a negative variance are NA with a medfit_warning_vcov_diagonal warning
n_clusters fewer than 50 clusters triggers a warning (a judgment, not a published cutoff) treat between results as rough
cross_level_equal paths constrained equal across levels (a, b, or both) with both equated the contrast is NA by constraint

Step 3: read the effects at each level 

nie(td)
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2446
nie(td, level = "between")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), between level: 0.5344
tidy(td, conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 15 × 5
   term            estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
   <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
 1 a_within           0.443    0.0495   0.346     0.540
 2 b_within           0.552    0.0506   0.453     0.651
 3 c_prime_within     0.268    0.0550   0.161     0.376
 4 a_between          0.559    0.0732   0.416     0.703
 5 b_between          0.955    0.194    0.575     1.34
 6 c_prime_between    0.229    0.134   -0.0331    0.491
 7 nie_within         0.245    0.0354   0.175     0.314
 8 nde_within         0.268    0.0550   0.161     0.376
 9 te_within          0.513    0.0571   0.401     0.625
10 pm_within          0.477    0.0697   0.340     0.613
11 nie_between        0.534    0.127    0.285     0.784
12 nde_between        0.229    0.134   -0.0331    0.491
13 te_between         0.763    0.0935   0.580     0.947
14 pm_between         0.700    0.163    0.380     1.02
15 nie_contrast      -0.290    0.137   -0.559    -0.0209

The within and between indirect effects are separate quantities: \(a_w b_w\) and \(a_b b_b\). Standard errors use the delta method over the joint covariance, so the covariance between a within and a between slope is part of every one. The intervals are Wald intervals.

Step 4: treat the contrast as descriptive

nie(td, level = "contrast") is the within effect minus the between effect. It is returned unless both a and b are equated across levels. It describes a difference between two quantities; it is not a test that the levels differ.

nie(td, level = "contrast")
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE), within - between contrast: -0.2899

Step 5: choose an interval

The delta-method interval from Step 3 is the default. When you want a distribution-based interval, use the cluster bootstrap: pass the lavaan fit to twolevel_statistic() and give bootstrap_mediation() the data and cluster =. Whole clusters are resampled and the model is refitted in every replicate. The example uses 30 replicates only to keep the page fast; use several hundred in a real analysis.

b <- bootstrap_mediation(
  twolevel_statistic(fit, "nie_between", treatment = "X", mediator = "M", outcome = "Y"),
  method = "nonparametric", data = d, cluster = "id", n_boot = 30, seed = 1
)
c(estimate = b@estimate, lower = b@ci_lower, upper = b@ci_upper, n_used = b@n_boot)
  estimate      lower      upper     n_used
 0.5344197  0.3379050  0.7479089 30.0000000

Report the percentile interval (ci_lower, ci_upper), not the standard deviation of the draws: refits with a negative between variance are kept, and at a few dozen clusters they give heavy tails. Replicates that fail are excluded and counted in a warning, so check n_boot in the result.

Step 6: report

State, at minimum: the number of clusters and the cluster sizes; the ICC of the treatment and the mediator; whether the fit was admissible; the within and between indirect effects with their intervals and the interval type; and, if you give the contrast, that it is descriptive. summary(td) prints the provenance of the fit and the assumptions in full.

glance(td)
# A tibble: 1 × 8
  nie_within nie_between nie_contrast n_clusters  nobs converged
       <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>      <int> <int> <lgl>
1      0.245       0.534       -0.290        100   500 TRUE
# ℹ 2 more variables: between_identified <lgl>, admissible <lgl>

When something goes wrong

Each condition carries a class. The Troubleshooting guide lists every two-level message with its cause and fix, and Which interval should I use? compares the interval types.
